doc.title: Pug Horton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 1998

chapter: Growing up with jazz in northern England
title: Her parents' taste in music
summary: Her parents liked popular songs of the 1930s, Gracie Fields and Noel Coward; she and Bob still listen to Gracie Fields.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Do you recall what kind of music your parents listened to?

Oh yes. My father’s favorite songs, one of the songs he sang was “The Music Goes Round and Round” and comes out here. My mother liked possibly the songs of Gracie Fields and sort of the songs that were on the radio. It was mostly the popular music of the ‘30s, Noel Coward and so on. Interestingly enough, we are very, Bobby and I listen to a lot of Gracie Fields. When Bob was asked about his favorite singers he said — not in jazz — one was Janet Baker and the great English — I suppose you’d call her an opera singer. And the other is Gracie Fields. And Gracie Fields didn’t have any musical training but has an incredible voice. And so that’s the kind of music that I was raised on. And that’s what my parents listened to.
